skim: Albertans began voting Monday on a historic referendum asking whether the province should pursue leaving Canada, with turnout expected near 80–85% and results due Tuesday morning.
A jury found Arm breached its licensing deal with Qualcomm, awarding a symbolic $2 in damages, while TSMC posted a record quarter and Anthropic's IPO valuation chatter slipped toward $1.5 trillion.

Zelensky said the war “must be brought to an end” after Trump's sanctions waiver on Russia, as Brent crude settled near $110 on Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks and GCC states invoked collective defense against the Houthis.
Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in an ODI tri-series opener, Arsenal edged Nottingham Forest, and Manchester United drew Leeds, while India opens a marathon New Zealand tour on Thursday.
In Mumbai, the jailed Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed a shooting targeting actor Tiger Shroff, and Qatar Museums opened the Fahad Bin Ali Palace to the public for the first time.

stories.headline: Albertans Vote On A Historic Referendum To Pursue Leaving Canada
stories.body: More than 1,400 polling stations opened across Alberta on Monday for a 10-question referendum, the centerpiece asking whether the province should remain in Canada or begin the legal process toward a binding separation vote. Elections Alberta expects turnout near 80–85% among nearly three million electors, with early results due after polls close at 8pm and a final count expected Tuesday morning. Per Global News (Oct 12) and The Canadian Press (Oct 11).

stories.headline: Fire At Canadian Military Base Kills Four Service Members
stories.body: A fast-moving fire tore through the training area at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta on Friday evening, killing four service members and injuring dozens more before spreading toward the surrounding municipal district. Prime Minister Mark Carney called it “one of the worst tragedies for forces on Canadian soil in peacetime,” as Edmonton hospitals declared a mass-casualty alert and the cause remained under investigation. Per TIME (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Albania’s Anti-Government Protests Turn Bloodier On Sixth Day
stories.body: Hundreds of students clashed with police outside Tirana’s Ministry of Education on Sunday with fireworks and at least one Molotov cocktail, as Albania’s protests stretched into a sixth day and the health ministry reported 65 new injuries—including 37 police officers—lifting the week’s toll to 272. Prime Minister Edi Rama again refused to resign, blamed a “foreign hand,” and warned the unrest could jeopardise Albania’s EU membership bid, even as he offered to discuss students’ “justified demands” over education costs. Per Al Jazeera (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Venezuela’s Opposition Closes Ranks Behind Machado, Demands Elections By 2027
stories.body: Members of Venezuela’s Unitary Democratic Platform meeting in Caracas on Sunday agreed to “recognise and support the leadership” of Nobel laureate María Corina Machado and released 14 proposals for a democratic transition, including freedom for political prisoners and the safe return of exiles. Machado, in exile since December, told the Financial Times she wants elections by July 2027, as a third round of government–opposition talks that exclude her continues under interim President Delcy Rodríguez. Per Al Jazeera (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Salman Ali Agha’s Century Powers Pakistan Past Sri Lanka In Tri-Series Opener
stories.body: Salman Ali Agha smashed 107 off 90 balls (10 fours, a six) to lift Pakistan to 305 all out, and Shaheen Afridi took 3-55 as Pakistan held off Sri Lanka’s reply of 268 all out to win the ODI tri-series opener in Rawalpindi, a series that also features England. Eshan Malinga took 4-46 for Sri Lanka. Per Daily Times (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Noni Madueke’s Late Strike Edges Arsenal Past Nottingham Forest
stories.body: Noni Madueke cut inside from the left in the 80th minute and his deflected effort beat Matz Sels to give Arsenal a win at the City Ground, keeping the Gunners within touching distance of leaders Manchester City. Forest, battling toward the relegation zone, had chances of their own in a scrappy afternoon before Madueke’s winner. Per Just Arsenal News (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Mbeumo Strike Not Enough As Leeds Peg Back Manchester United
stories.body: Bryan Mbeumo put Manchester United ahead at Elland Road before Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised shortly after half-time, the two sides sharing the points in a contest that leaves both clubs mid-table. Referee Darren England and VAR Peter Bankes oversaw the draw. Per match coverage (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Nasdaq Posts Worst Week Since June As AI-Debt Fears Widen
stories.body: The Nasdaq Composite fell 4.5% for the week—its worst stretch since June—as a credit-stress scare around AI-infrastructure borrowers pushed money out of megacap tech and into value shares; the S&P 500 lost 1.9% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.7% on rotation into financials and industrials. Semiconductors extended a multi-session slide. Per Mitrade (Oct 19).

stories.headline: Hot September Inflation Revives Bets On A Fed Rate Hike
stories.body: US headline CPI rose 0.6% month-on-month and 3.7% year-on-year in September, with core CPI up 0.3% and 2.6%, both above forecasts, reviving expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise rates at its late-October meeting. Per Mitrade (Oct 19).

stories.headline: Brent Nears $110 As Hormuz Attacks Collide With Reserve Releases
stories.body: Brent crude briefly touched $110 a barrel and settled near that level—its highest close since May—after the IRGC targeted at least four ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend and Ukraine kept striking Russian energy infrastructure. The IEA and the US moved to release strategic reserves, while Exxon and Chevron hit record highs. Per Invezz (Oct 18) and Mitrade (Oct 19).

stories.headline: TSMC Posts Record Quarter As AI Chip Demand Outruns Capacity
stories.body: TSMC reported Q3 revenue of $46.7 billion, up 41% year-on-year, with high-performance/AI computing chips making up 68% of sales; it guided Q4 revenue to $52.3–54.3 billion, roughly 58% growth at the midpoint. CEO C.C. Wei said AI accelerator demand is “still far above our capability today to supply” and that the company’s multiyear growth forecast “probably will be higher.” Per The Motley Fool (Oct 18).

stories.headline: CoreWeave’s Credit Stress Deepens As AI-Debt Fears Spread
stories.body: CoreWeave shares fell sharply over five sessions as its 2031 bonds briefly yielded more than 16% and the cost of insuring its debt rose above 1,000 basis points, with investors questioning whether its roughly $50 billion debt load can be serviced. The stress spilled into data-centre and AI-infrastructure shares broadly. Per Mitrade (Oct 19).

stories.headline: Anthropic’s IPO Valuation Talk Slips To $1.5 Trillion As Growth Cools
stories.body: Investors are now discussing a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation for Anthropic’s planned Nasdaq listing, down from the $2 trillion once expected, after Q3 revenue of $16.8 billion—up 45% from $11.6 billion in Q2—showed sequential growth slowing. Marketing could begin as early as Nov 9, led by Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, with a listing targeted before Nov 26. Per Reuters, via ValueAddVC (Oct 15).

stories.headline: Zelensky Says War ‘Must Be Brought To An End’ As Russia Hails Sanctions Waiver
stories.body: Hours after Trump’s Friday order waived nearly all Lindsey Graham Act sanctions and tariffs on Russia—including threatened 500% tariffs on Russian goods and 100% secondary tariffs on buyers of its oil and gas—Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it a “significant and truly historic moment” that averted a “complete standstill” in US-Russia economic ties; Russia then launched a large overnight strike on Ukraine’s energy and industrial sites. Zelensky said in a Sunday post the war “must be brought to an end,” citing “virtually nonstop communication” with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and thanking the US for resuming intelligence-sharing. Per Al Jazeera (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Israeli Election Polls Show Eisenkot’s Yashar Ahead, Blocs Still Short Of Majority
stories.body: Four fresh polls (Maariv, Channel 13, Kan and Channel 12) all show Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar ahead of Likud, but neither bloc reaches the 61 seats needed, nine days before the Oct 27 vote; the four-poll average puts the opposition at 51.25 seats against Netanyahu’s bloc’s 51, with Yashar at 21.5 and Likud down to 19. Per The Jerusalem Post (Oct 18).

fixtures.headline: India’s Tour Of New Zealand Begins
fixtures.body: India opens a marathon 12-match tour (five T20Is, five ODIs, two Tests) with the first T20I at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, running into the World Test Championship cycle.

fixtures.headline: El Clásico Returns To Camp Nou
fixtures.body: Barcelona hosts Real Madrid in the season’s first Clásico, a night kickoff at Camp Nou with major La Liga title-race implications.

fixtures.headline: Mexico City Grand Prix
fixtures.body: F1 heads to the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez for the Mexico City Grand Prix, the next round in a tightening title fight after Austin.

portfolio.headline: Arm Loses Key Claims To Qualcomm In Licensing Breach Trial
portfolio.body: A Delaware jury found Arm breached its licensing agreement with Qualcomm by failing to supply promised software patches and design tools, and that Arm intentionally interfered with Qualcomm’s relationship with Meta—awarding Qualcomm a symbolic $2 in total damages. Judge Maryellen Noreika must still rule on whether Qualcomm can stop paying Arm royalties for five years, a clause Arm calls unenforceable; Qualcomm said Arm “intentionally acted to disrupt Qualcomm’s businesses,” while Arm said it “operated in good faith.” Per The Star/Reuters (Oct 14).

portfolio.headline: Oracle’s AI-Debt Scrutiny Deepens Into A Second Week
portfolio.body: Oracle remains under pressure as its roughly $130 billion debt load—built on a $25 billion bond sale earlier this year—keeps drawing scrutiny following S&P’s downgrade of its issuer rating to BBB–, one notch above junk, over an “uncertain path to profitability.” No fresh company-specific announcement surfaced Monday; Oracle is riding the same AI-infrastructure debt jitters that dragged the Nasdaq to its worst week since June. Per S&P rating action (Jul 2026) and Mitrade (Oct 19).

portfolio.headline: Intel Slides Toward Its Oct 29 Report As Chip Stocks Stay Under Pressure
portfolio.body: Intel shares have fallen sharply from their September high as chip stocks extend their slide into the company’s Oct 29 earnings report, the next scheduled test of whether AI-driven demand can offset investor nerves about infrastructure spending. Per 247wallst.com (Oct 13) and Tikr (Oct 2026).

portfolio.headline: CrowdStrike Falls With Cloud-Security Peers, No Fresh Trigger Found
portfolio.body: CrowdStrike dropped alongside the broader cybersecurity and cloud complex as the AI-infrastructure debt scare that hit Wall Street last week continued to weigh on richly-valued software names; no company-specific news or analyst action was found behind Monday’s move. Per market data (Oct 19).

portfolio.headline: Palantir Slides Again As The AI-Infrastructure Rout Runs Into A New Week
portfolio.body: Palantir fell for another session with no distinct company announcement behind the move—its recent run of government contract wins continued separately, but the stock is still being swept up in the broader AI-infrastructure debt worries pressuring high-multiple tech names. Per market data (Oct 19).

portfolio.headline: Twilio Leads The Watchlist’s Declines As Cloud Names Keep Sliding
portfolio.body: Twilio led the watchlist’s declines Monday, with no company-specific news found to explain the move; the slide tracks a broader selloff in cloud and developer-infrastructure stocks now running into its second week. Per market data (Oct 19).

portfolio.headline: Figma Slides With Other Recently-Listed Software Names
portfolio.body: Figma fell with no verified company-specific catalyst found for the session, caught in the same risk-off mood hitting other richly-valued, recently-public software names as investors reassess how AI-infrastructure spending will be financed. Per market data (Oct 19).

portfolio.headline: Ring Energy Rises As Crude Nears $110 On Hormuz Tanker Attacks
portfolio.body: Ring Energy, a small-cap Permian producer with high sensitivity to spot crude, rose as Brent crude settled near $110 a barrel—its highest close since May—after the IRGC targeted tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend; no company-specific announcement was found, and the move tracks the broader oil rally covered elsewhere in this edition. Per Invezz (Oct 18) and Mitrade (Oct 19).

stories.headline: Rubio Says US Will Review Russia-Sanctions Waiver On India’s Oil Imports Within 60 Days
stories.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington will use a 60-day window to review waivers under the new Russia sanctions law before deciding on tariffs against major buyers of Russian energy, days after Trump signed an order temporarily shielding India and China from the Lindsey Graham Act’s tariffs of up to 100%. Rubio said India has “voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia,” calling it an important ally; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added that European allies “refused” to join US secondary tariffs on India and China. Per WION (Oct 18); Rubio visits Mumbai next week to meet EAM Jaishankar.

stories.headline: Stones And Bricks Hurled At J&K-Bound Bus In Haryana, Omar Abdullah Demands Action
stories.body: A Delhi-Srinagar sleeper bus was attacked with stones and bricks at a dhaba in Haryana’s Karnal district on the night of Oct 17 after a parking dispute, shattering windows and injuring an elderly passenger; the driver alleged attackers tore off the bus’s number plate and declared J&K-registered vehicles unwelcome in Haryana, calling it “sheer hooliganism.” Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah’s office took up the matter with the Haryana government, which promised “prompt and stringent action.” Per WION (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Lawrence Bishnoi Gang Claims Shooting At Tiger Shroff Over Salman Khan Ties
stories.body: Three men on a motorcycle fired at Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu on Sunday evening; Shroff was unhurt but his driver was shot in the hand. A caller identifying as part of the jailed Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility in an audio clip, saying Shroff was targeted for continuing to work with Salman Khan “despite the gang’s directions,” warning “anyone... who works with Salman Khan, we will kill him.” Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis directed Mumbai Police to expedite the probe. Per WION (Oct 19).

stories.headline: Healey Weighs Income Tax On Family Business Handovers In Budget Raid
stories.body: Chancellor John Healey is considering taxing family business handovers to the next generation as income rather than capital gains, which could nearly double the bill—an owner passing down a £1m firm via “redeemable shares” could pay £450,000 instead of £240,000. Accountant John Endacott warned it risks “taxing them to extinction,” while shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said the plan would make it “easier to sell a family business than to pass it on to your own children.” The IFS says Healey may need “tens of billions” in new taxes to close a £35bn shortfall ahead of the Oct 28 Budget. Per The Telegraph via AOL (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Burnham Puts AI At Centre Of Push For Closer EU Ties
stories.body: PM Andy Burnham plans to make AI central to a reset with Brussels at next month’s summit, lobbying for British firms to get “trusted access” to an EU scheme prioritising sovereign tech investment—without it, UK companies risk exclusion from AI contracts worth tens of billions of euros under the upcoming EU Cloud and AI Development Act. techUK warns the rules could shut British firms out of a €47bn tech market; Synthesia’s Alexandru Voicu said the draft was “drafted by EU lawyers for EU lawyers instead of the real world.” Burnham has called stronger single-market ties his “duty.” Per The Telegraph via AOL (Oct 18).

stories.headline: GCC Condemns Houthi Attacks As Riyadh Tower Shuts Offices, Egypt Weighs Defence Role
stories.body: GCC foreign ministers meeting in Manama condemned repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and declared an attack on any member would be treated as an attack on all six under their joint defence pact, as the coalition intercepted drones near Riyadh and the Eastern Province. Riyadh’s 99-storey Kingdom Centre—whose tenants include Merrill Lynch, McKinsey and the IMF—ordered staff to work remotely “until further notice,” a week after a Houthi strike on Riyadh’s main airport killed 13. Egypt’s parliament held an emergency session after President Sisi sought authorisation to help defend Saudi Arabia, saying “we are speaking only about defence.” Per Al Jazeera and Malay Mail/AFP (Oct 18).

stories.headline: Qatar Museums Opens Fahad Bin Ali Palace To The Public For The First Time
stories.body: Doha’s Fahad Bin Ali Palace, built 1952-63 near the Amiri Diwan, opened to the public for the first time as a venue for two new exhibitions running Oct 26 to May 2027: “Wooden Doors of Qatar,” showing 52 historic doors from the National Museum’s collection, and “Atharna 2026,” presenting pre-Islamic burial-mound finds from Al Thakhira. National Museum director Sheikh Abdulaziz bin Hamad Al-Thani said the doors “preserve an important record of Qatar’s architectural and social history.” Per The Peninsula (Oct 18).

doha_events.headline: Qatar World Cup 10-Ball 2026
doha_events.body: The international 10-ball pool championship opens today at Ezdan Palace Hotel.

doha_events.headline: Milipol Qatar 2026
doha_events.body: The 16th edition of the homeland security and safety exhibition opens Tuesday at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Center with over 270 companies and seven international pavilions, alongside the Doha International Conference on AI and Security.

doha_events.headline: MOQ Drift Show 2026
doha_events.body: A motorsport drifting show takes over Mall of Qatar.

doha_events.headline: Moscow Ballet La Classique: Swan Lake
doha_events.body: The Russian touring company performs the classic ballet at Al Mayassa Theater, Qatar National Convention Centre.

doha_events.headline: Qatar International Baja 2026
doha_events.body: The cross-country rally event runs at Lusail International Circuit.
